trust_decision.summary: At restricted-compile time the transformer decides whether a name may be bound in restricted code: any name starting with '_' (except the bare '_') is rejected so it cannot shadow an injected guard global such as _getattr_, _getitem_, _write_ or _print_. The decision lives in RestrictingNodeTransformer.check_name (transformer.py:374-387) and is applied to function/lambda parameter lists by check_function_argument_names (transformer.py:389-401); at the pinned commit that helper iterates only args, vararg, kwarg and kwonlyargs, so positional-only parameters (ast.arguments.posonlyargs) are never validated.

landing_point.why: The summary says guard hooks can be shadowed via positional-only arguments, so a reader opens check_function_argument_names - the one helper that validates parameter names - and sees that it walks args, vararg, kwarg and kwonlyargs but not the posonlyargs list that sits first in every ast.arguments node.

fix_sites.entry_point: RestrictedPython.compile.compile_restricted / compile_restricted_exec / compile_restricted_eval / compile_restricted_single (source text, reaching RestrictingNodeTransformer.visit_FunctionDef at transformer.py:1131 and visit_Lambda at transformer.py:1140) and RestrictedPython.compile.compile_restricted_function (parameter string, compile.py:161-162, whose synthetic def is visited by the same handlers) - 2 distinct input routes
fix_sites.module_kind: restricted-code compiler policy (ast.NodeTransformer in the transformer package module)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: A solver can argue the parameters string handed to compile_restricted_function is written by the trusted application, and positional-only syntax is a niche 3.8+ form, so only source text passed to compile_restricted_exec with a plain `def` is an untrusted surface - leaving the lambda and parameter-string shapes unverified.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: The bare name `_` is explicitly legal everywhere (check_name only errors when name != '_'), so `def f(_, /)` and `lambda _, /: 1` must keep compiling, and each parameter kind must still produce exactly one error message because tests assert the exact error tuple - a fix that rejects every positional-only parameter, or that also runs the check from visit_arguments, breaks legitimate code and doubles the error count.

O6_input_shapes: positional-only parameter with a default, `def foo(_bad=1, /)` (fix.diff:49-52)
positional-only parameter in a lambda, `f = lambda _bad, /: None` (fix.diff:61-64)
positional-only parameter mixed with plain parameters, `def foo(good, _bad, /)` or `def foo(good, /, _bad)` (the second half already handled by node.args.args)
positional-only parameter with an annotation, `def foo(_bad: int, /)` - same code path, not in the published tests
parameters supplied as a string to compile_restricted_function, e.g. p='_bad, /', which becomes a synthetic def and is validated by the same helper (src/RestrictedPython/compile.py:161-162)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A wrapper that builds the restricted function's ast.arguments node directly with ast.arg objects instead of parsing a `def` header string, so the parameter names never pass through ast.parse.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: This module already synthesises a FunctionDef from a parameter string and renames it after the fact at compile.py:167, so a second builder that skips the source text is a natural extension - and a check placed in visit_arguments/visit_arg would have to still fire.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: The same underscore-prefix rule is already duplicated inline for attribute names (`node.attr.startswith('_') and node.attr != '_'`); a sibling would be a third copy of the rule, e.g. for keyword-argument names in visit_keyword (transformer.py:788-792), which currently checks nothing.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The attribute check re-implements check_name's rule instead of calling it, so a maintainer could equally have written a separate positional-parameter check inside visit_FunctionDef rather than in the shared helper.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Validation inside visit_arguments/visit_arg, which today only recurse, so every ast.arguments node is checked once regardless of whether it came from def, lambda or a synthetic wrapper.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: These two no-op visitors are the obvious place to put argument validation; the current split is exactly why the posonlyargs field was missed.

O9_family: incomplete denylist / incomplete list of disallowed inputs (CWE-184): the forbidden-name check covers only some parameter kinds, letting an injected guard name be shadowed

O10_build.toolchain: setuptools >= 78.1.1 via pyproject.toml (build-backend setuptools.build_meta), requires-python >=3.10,<3.16; pytest + pytest-mock for tests; tox.ini drives the envs
O10_build.project_tests: tests/transformer/test_functiondef.py and tests/transformer/test_lambda.py (one exact-error-tuple test per parameter kind: args, defaulted args, *args, **kwargs, `*`-only), tests/transformer/test_name.py, tests/test_compile.py and tests/test_compile_restricted_function.py for the compile APIs

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Add the posonlyargs loop inline in visit_FunctionDef only (leaving lambda and the compile_restricted_function parameter string aside), or reject every positional-only parameter instead of reusing check_name, which also drops the `_` exception.
